claims.text: Nearly equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles begin as a chemically disordered FCC solid solution.
The configurational entropy of an equiatomic five-element alloy approaches R ln 5.
High configurational entropy lowers the thermodynamic driving force for precipitation and phase separation.
Configurational entropy thermodynamically stabilizes the FCC phase of CoCrFeMnNi.
Severe lattice distortion and chemical complexity produce sluggish diffusion by creating high barriers for atomic jumps.
Atomic diffusion coefficients in the nanoparticles will be one to two orders of magnitude below those of conventional alloys.
Unlike traditional alloys, whose diffusion is driven primarily by vacancy concentration and temperature, HENA diffusion is controlled by the sluggish-diffusion effect.
Surface-energy minimization drives nanoparticle grain growth and shape change at elevated temperature.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations affect phase stability, stacking-fault energy, and FCC-HCP interfacial energy in CoCrFeMnNi.
The FCC phase is stable from cryogenic through moderate temperatures.
Increasing temperature causes the stacking-fault energy to increase, suppressing stacking faults and nanotwins.
Increasing temperature causes longitudinal spin fluctuations to lower the stacking-fault energy and promote stacking faults or an FCC-to-HCP transition.
Nanoparticle surface stress alters the bulk FCC-HCP phase boundary.
High configurational entropy raises the activation energy for precipitation and diffusion.
CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles will be more thermally stable than binary or ternary alloys and will avoid secondary-phase precipitation up to temperatures at which bulk alloys decompose.
Entropy stabilization shifts the onset of FCC-to-HCP transformation or grain growth to higher temperature.
Below 10 nm, surface effects may cause amorphization or rapid grain growth.
Binary and ternary transition-metal alloys generally exhibit faster diffusion, earlier precipitation, and lower thermal stability because they have lower configurational entropy.
Intrinsic entropy stabilization fails below a critical particle size when surface energy dominates bulk Gibbs free energy.
Significant deviation from equiatomic composition reduces configurational entropy and can permit ordering or phase separation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis states that increasing temperature lowers stacking-fault energy and promotes stacking faults or HCP formation, whereas the mechanism states that stacking-fault energy increases with temperature and suppresses stacking faults and nanotwins.
